name: Yüan-ti
bio: Yüan-ti (AD 508–554) is represented by a seven-line poem, “The Rejected Wife,” in which a woman meets her successor and her former husband in the same hour.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: The Rejected Wife
poems.author: Yüan-ti
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
Entering the Hall, she meets the new wife:
Leaving the gate, she runs into her former husband.
Words stick: she does not manage to say anything:
She presses her hands together and hesitates.
Agitates moon-like fan--sheds pearl-like tears--
Realizes she loves him just as much as ever:
That her present pain will never come to an end.
